source: Stab and Gurevych (2017) Parsing Argumentation Structures in Persuasive Essays
finding: Annotators reliably find major claims and premises in essays but disagree most on claims.
numbers: 80 essays. Major claim: agreement 97.9%, kappa .877, unitized alpha .810. Premise: kappa .833, alpha .824. Claim: kappa .635, alpha .524.
limits: Claim vs premise is the main confusion; one annotator often did not split sentences holding a claim. Essays only, trained annotators.
agent_relevance: Claim detection is the weak link in restating a claim with grounds; expect noise there.

source: Stab and Gurevych (2017) Parsing Argumentation Structures in Persuasive Essays
finding: Human upper bound on structure parsing for components, relations, stance.
numbers: Human macro F1: components .868, relation identification .854, stance .844. ILP joint model reaches 95.2%, 87.9%, 80.5% of human level.
limits: Persuasive essays; trees only (each premise has one target). Even humans cap near .85, so gold diagrams are not unique.
agent_relevance: Do not treat one diagram as ground truth; compare with a tolerance.

source: Stab and Gurevych (2017) Parsing Argumentation Structures in Persuasive Essays
finding: Joint inference over components and links beats separate classifiers.
numbers: ILP joint model improved claim F1 by .071 and linked-pair F1 by .077 over base classifiers. Essays component F1: base .794, joint .826, heuristic .759.
limits: Essays and microtexts only.
agent_relevance: Use code-side consistency checks on the diagram (every premise has a target) instead of trusting each model label.

source: Stab and Gurevych (2017) Parsing Argumentation Structures in Persuasive Essays
finding: Authors argue linked vs convergent need not be separated during structure identification.
numbers: Cites Freeman 2011 (distinction often ambiguous in everyday text), Yanal 1991 (equals several separate arguments), Conway 1991 (linked can be omitted). Linking equals grouping premises.
limits: Design choice by the authors, not an experiment. Their model drops linked/convergent labels.
agent_relevance: Do not force a linked/convergent label in S2; record premise groups only when a check needs them.

source: Stab and Gurevych (2017) Parsing Argumentation Structures in Persuasive Essays
finding: Unlinked premises are a large error source.
numbers: Relation model leaves 37.1% of premises unlinked in the model selection data. Not-linked pairs were 17.5% of training pairs and 16.5% of test pairs.
limits: Corpus-specific.
agent_relevance: After diagramming, code should flag premises with no target.

source: Habernal and Gurevych (2017) Argumentation Mining in User-Generated Web Discourse
finding: Toulmin-style annotation of web discourse has only moderate agreement.
numbers: 340 documents, six education topics. Persuasiveness filter Fleiss kappa .59 (990 docs). Toulmin token-level joint Krippendorff alpha_U .48. Sequence labelling beat baseline .156 (p<.001).
limits: Modified Toulmin model (claim, premise, backing, rebuttal, refutation). Informal web text.
agent_relevance: Toulmin roles (warrant, backing, rebuttal) are hard to label reliably; keep the schema small.

source: Habernal and Gurevych (2017) Argumentation Mining in User-Generated Web Discourse
finding: Agreement depends on register and topic.
numbers: Alpha_U .59 in comments and .69 in forum posts, but .22 in articles and .24 in blog posts. By topic: prayer in schools .68, private vs public schools .44, redshirting .14, mainstreaming .08.
limits: Same annotators across registers. Boundary: informal, implicit or opinion-heavy texts break standardisation.
agent_relevance: Expect weak S1/S2 output on rhetorical text; lower trust there.

source: Habernal et al. (2018) The Argument Reasoning Comprehension Task
finding: Humans find the hidden warrant with training-dependent accuracy.
numbers: 173 AMT workers, 100 test questions. Mean 79.8%; with extensive formal training in reasoning, logic or argumentation 90.9% (SD .114); education alone had negligible effect; topic familiarity not significant.
limits: Two-choice task (pick the correct warrant), chance 50%.
agent_relevance: Skill comes from training in argument, not schooling; an explicit scaffold may stand in for it.

source: Habernal et al. (2018) The Argument Reasoning Comprehension Task
finding: Early neural models were at chance on choosing the implicit warrant.
numbers: Test accuracy: random .491, language model .500, attention .513, intra-warrant attention .556, with context .560 (best). Humans .798 / .909. Data: 1,210 train, 316 dev, 444 test.
limits: 2018 models.
agent_relevance: Baseline for how far LLMs have moved (see Ku 2025).

source: Habernal et al. (2018) The Argument Reasoning Comprehension Task
finding: A warrant fits only relative to the stated claim; training was doubled with permuted opposite-claim copies.
numbers: Each instance has warrant W for claim C and alternative AW for the opposite claim; permuted copies (R,C,W1,W0) added, and performance rose (figure not read).
limits: Dataset built so the warrant flips with the claim.
agent_relevance: When restating, test the hidden premise against the opposite claim; if it fits both, it is doing no work.

source: Ku et al. (2025) Multi-Agent LLM Debate Unveils the Premise Left Unsaid
finding: A single zero-shot LLM beats earlier neural models on implicit-premise choice.
numbers: ARCT (SemEval-2018) test set. Single-agent LLM accuracy .7928 vs LSTM .7050 and fine-tuned RoBERTa .7564 (reproduced by authors); random .5000.
limits: Binary choice, not free generation. Model name not recorded in text read.
agent_relevance: Offer candidates to choose between rather than ask the model to invent.

source: Ku et al. (2025) Multi-Agent LLM Debate Unveils the Premise Left Unsaid
finding: Two debating LLM agents raise accuracy only if each may pick its own stance.
numbers: Chosen&Sequential .8694; Chosen&Simultaneous .8446; both beat single agent (McNemar p<.0001 and p<.01). Cochran Q=101.03, df=4, p<.0001.
limits: Max 10 rounds, temperature .5, no CoT or few-shot. Gain came from agents revising after opposing views, not repeated sampling.
agent_relevance: Same-model agents are not independent (G4); treat the gain as a hint to test.

source: Ku et al. (2025) Multi-Agent LLM Debate Unveils the Premise Left Unsaid
finding: Forcing an assigned stance hurts.
numbers: Given-stance debates were worse than single agent: Given&Sequential p<.0001 (275 both correct, 77 single only, 35 given only, 57 both wrong); Given&Simultaneous p<.01 (288, 64, 32, 60).
limits: Same dataset. Assigned positions cause rigid defence of a wrong premise.
agent_relevance: Supports no persona voters (G4); do not assign sides to force alternatives.

source: Gorur, Rago, Toni (2024) Can LLMs perform Relation-based Argument Mining?
finding: Primed open LLMs beat a RoBERTa baseline on support/attack between argument texts.
numbers: 10 datasets. Macro F1: Llama-70B-4bit 75, Mixtral-8x7B-4bit 73, Mistral-7B 70, Llama-13B 62, Llama-13B-4bit 64; RoBERTa baseline 68. Inference 1.73 s (Llama-70B) vs 0.005 s (RoBERTa).
limits: Binary task only (no 'no relation'); English only; attack F1 lower than support for all models.
agent_relevance: Support/attack labels are within LLM reach; attack is the weak side.

source: Gorur, Rago, Toni (2024) Can LLMs perform Relation-based Argument Mining?
finding: Results vary widely by dataset.
numbers: Microtexts support/attack/avg F1: Llama-70B 96/95/96 vs RoBERTa 67/67/67. Nixon-Kennedy Llama-70B 64/71/68 vs RoBERTa 56/67/62; CDCP Llama-13B attack F1 12.
limits: Table text partly garbled in PDF extraction.
agent_relevance: Do not trust one benchmark number; the same model swings widely across datasets.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Exploring the Potential of LLMs in Computational Argumentation
finding: Zero-shot LLMs do decently on argument mining, but not all models do.
numbers: 11 argument mining datasets, McNemar tests. GPT-3.5-Turbo and Flan-UL2 beat random in most tasks; Llama-2-13B fell below random in most, notably FEVER stance and evidence classification.
limits: Zero-shot; 2023 models. Flan-UL2 better on binary tasks, GPT-3.5 on multi-class.
agent_relevance: Weak models can be worse than chance on fine labels.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Exploring the Potential of LLMs in Computational Argumentation
finding: A few demonstrations close the gap with fine-tuned models.
numbers: With fewer than 10 demonstrations LLMs matched fine-tuned PLMs trained on 500 samples. Llama-2-7B beat 13B on simple tasks.
limits: Gap to full-train fine-tuned models remained.
agent_relevance: Use a handful of worked standardisation examples in S2 prompts.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Exploring the Potential of LLMs in Computational Argumentation
finding: End-to-end beat a mine-then-generate pipeline on counter-speech.
numbers: End-to-end outperformed the pipeline on all 3 metrics; pipeline lost information in the intermediate step.
limits: Generation task, not diagramming.
agent_relevance: Keep the original text available when working from the diagram.

source: Pirozelli et al. (2026) An LLM-Based System for Argument Mining
finding: An LLM pipeline recovers textbook argument structure well on a small set.
numbers: 42 short textbook arguments (mean 332 characters). Conclusion detection accuracy 92.50%. Span detection P 80.31, R 72.87, F1 75.70. Relation accuracy 80.57%.
limits: Gold diagrams from one author; wording differences accepted. Implicit conclusions were not handled.
agent_relevance: Conclusion finding is the strongest step; implicit conclusions fail.

source: Pirozelli et al. (2026) An LLM-Based System for Argument Mining
finding: Human raters scored structure and implicit premises high on a 1-3 scale.
numbers: Mean (exact agreement): span 2.86 (.95), conclusion 2.90 (.88), relation 2.85 (.80), structure 2.96 (.97), implicit premises 2.92 (.88).
limits: Lenient scoring, ceiling effect; kappa not reported due to skew.
agent_relevance: Looks good under lenient grading; not proof of exact match.

source: Pirozelli et al. (2026) An LLM-Based System for Argument Mining
finding: On benchmarks the full pipeline fails under strict span match but is much better with gold spans.
numbers: AbstRCT full pipeline span F1 59.65, link F1 20.82 vs Morio 2022 70.93, 39.74. AAEC full pipeline link F1 0.41 vs 55.72. With gold components AbstRCT link F1 51.51 (+11.77 over SOTA), relation 46.21 (+7.5); AAEC span 85.20.
limits: Models GPT-4.1, GPT-5, GPT-5-mini; exact span matching punishes small shifts.
agent_relevance: The bottleneck is where a span starts and ends; fix spans by code and let the model only label.

source: Ryu et al. (2026) Argument Reconstruction as Supervision for Critical Thinking in LLMs
finding: Training on reconstructions (GAAR/Arguinas) helped some critical-thinking tasks, not all.
numbers: Qwen3-4B-Base pre-adaptation: ReClor accuracy 78.28 to 84.48; UKPConvArg2 92.45 to 92.49; WebisCMV20 55.45 to 53.30. Continued tuning raised WebisArgQuality20 F1 by 51.3% on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
limits: Fine-tuning, not prompting. Table rows partly garbled in extraction; some cells fell.
agent_relevance: Reconstruction helps logic tasks in some conditions; not a universal win.

source: Ryu et al. (2026) Argument Reconstruction as Supervision for Critical Thinking in LLMs
finding: Reconstruction quality depends on the engine; about 41% of premises are implicit.
numbers: Validity / faithfulness win rate: LLM prompting 40.8/26.4, gpt-oss-120b 39.2/32.1, Claude Sonnet 4.5 no-think 51.7/46.2, Sonnet think 80.8/48.8. Implicit premises 40.94%; LLMs write fewer implicit premises than humans.
limits: Judge is Claude Sonnet 4.5 (human check: 99.0% NL-to-FOL, 89.5% pairwise).
agent_relevance: Validity and faithfulness differ; check validity with a solver, not with model opinion (G2/G3).

source: Ryu et al. (2026) Argument Reconstruction as Supervision for Critical Thinking in LLMs
finding: Fallacies, LLM-made text and long arguments in training data hurt.
numbers: Fallacious arguments detrimental; human-written arguments most positive; arguments over 290 words or 9+ premises degrade results; high implicit ratio helps ArgRC, low helps ReClor.
limits: Only 10.8% of downstream arguments are long.
agent_relevance: Keep restated arguments short (few premises).

source: Survey (2025) Large Language Models in Argument Mining: A Survey
finding: Survey of 250 LLM argument-mining papers: implicit claims remain weak; fewer labels raise agreement.
numbers: Corpus 250 papers; UKP essay segmentation reached kappa .81 by focusing annotators on two labels.
limits: Review; no new experiments. Read partly by keyword.
agent_relevance: Fewer roles, better reliability.

source: Dwyer, Hogan, Stewart (2012) Argument mapping and critical thinking in e-learning
finding: An 8-week argument-mapping course raised critical-thinking scores more than no instruction.
numbers: 74 psychology undergraduates, AM course vs no-instruction control, Halpern assessment pre/post. AM group improved on overall and every subscale and gained more than control on overall and argument analysis.
limits: Only the abstract page read; no effect sizes shown. Single course, single group.
agent_relevance: Human evidence that making structure visible trains argument analysis.

source: Wikipedia (accessed 2026) Argument map
finding: Reported gain from mapping-based critical-thinking courses is about 0.70 SD.
numbers: Cited to Alvarez (2007) M.A. thesis; about twice the gain of standard critical-thinking courses. Maps can raise cognitive load and need coaching (Nussbaum 2012).
limits: Secondary source; a search snippet gave 0.8 SD attributed to van Gelder, unverified. Thesis not opened.
agent_relevance: Mapping helps humans with coaching but costs load.

source: Wikipedia (accessed 2026) Argument map
finding: Definitions and disputes on linked vs convergent.
numbers: Thomas (1973) introduced 'linked'; linked premises need each other, convergent premises support independently; terminology and root position of the conclusion are disputed.
limits: Encyclopedia summary.
agent_relevance: Treat the label as a tag, not ground truth.

source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Informal Logic
finding: Standard recipe for standardisation and the minimal-premise rule.
numbers: Remove noise, restate questions, clarify vague claims, recover unstated parts; implicit premise should be the 'logically minimum' weakest bridge; indicator words are neither necessary nor sufficient.
limits: First 100000 of 132909 characters read. Natural-language deductivism criticised by Johnson (2000) and Godden (2004) as artificial.
agent_relevance: Gives a clear S1/S2 template: key-component table, then arrows.
